importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation across sub-types — warehouse PEB, aircraft hangar, cold storage, multi-storey, and open shed are visually distinct structures. Buyers scan images first to confirm the building type matches their project requirement before reading any specs.

Building type, clear span, eave height, and frame type are primary shortlisting criteria for project-specific procurement. Without matching specs, buyers cannot evaluate whether the seller can execute their specific project.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Recognised brands — Tata BlueScope, Pennar Industries, Kirby India, Zamil Steel, Everest Industries — carry significant buyer trust signals; architects, EPC contractors, and institutional buyers actively specify or prefer named manufacturers.
importance_ranking.reason: Turnkey PEB procurement involves design liability, IS code compliance, erection capability, and post-erection warranty — buyers evaluate manufacturer credentials, track record, and certification before shortlisting. Seller identity is a primary trust gate for capital construction projects.

Every PEB project is custom-scoped — span, height, cladding, crane load, and site conditions all affect the final price. Listed per-sq-ft rates are indicative budget entry points; final price is always project-quoted after design. Indian buyers use visible rates for initial budget sanity checks but do not shortlist on price alone.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Component/fabrication-only suppliers quote per MT; portable cabin suppliers quote per piece. Per sq ft is dominant for turnkey PEB projects and must be shown to prevent misreading against per-MT or per-piece listings.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per MT vs per piece creates genuine price comparison confusion across listing types in this MCAT. Unit must be shown alongside any indicative price so buyers can compare like-for-like.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Building type (warehouse vs hangar vs cold storage vs factory) is non-interchangeable — each demands a distinct structural system, load design, and cladding specification, driving the largest price delta across all spec dimensions.

Frame type (clear span vs multi-span vs lean-to vs mono slope) directly determines the structural steel tonnage and primary frame cost — a clear-span 60 m frame commands a significant premium over a multi-span equivalent covering the same area.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Clear span (column-free width) is the single most critical structural parameter buyers specify — it determines whether the building can accommodate their equipment, vehicles, or operational layout, and drives primary steel tonnage and cost.

Crane-compatible PEB frames (EOT crane provision) require reinforced columns, runway beams, and higher eave heights — a fundamentally different and more expensive structural system that buyers in manufacturing and logistics must confirm upfront.

Insulation specification (none, glasswool, PUF sandwich panel) is a primary cost and thermal performance differentiator — cold storage and temperature-controlled facilities require specific insulation that doubles or triples cladding cost.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Structure type (PEB vs open shed vs closed vs G+1) defines the fundamental building system a seller must design and supply — sellers cannot determine structural scope, material tonnage, or price without this.

Built-up area is the primary project scale signal — it directly determines steel tonnage, cladding quantity, and total project cost, enabling sellers to assess feasibility and provide an indicative rate.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the building is a warehouse, factory, cold storage, or hangar to determine the correct structural loads, cladding system, and compliance requirements before responding with a price.
